title: Collect every VCF Installer task in deterministic order
prompt:
Implement `vcfinstaller/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go client that retrieves the complete VMware Cloud Foundation Installer 9.1 task collection. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file. Before implementing, research the `getTasks` operation in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewClient(baseURL, accessToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).ListAllTasks(ctx context.Context, options ListTasksOptions) ([]Task, error)`, `Task`, `ListTasksOptions`, `APIError`, and `ProtocolError`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject a non-HTTP(S) service-root URL, a blank or header-unsafe access token, a nil context, and a `PageSize` outside 1 through the specification maximum of 100. Errors must not disclose the access token.

Every bodyless request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` and one `Accept: application/json`. It has no `Content-Type`, body, transfer encoding, or positive content length. The first request sends `pageSize` but omits `pageNumber`; subsequent requests send the next one-based `pageNumber` reported by the preceding page and the same `pageSize`. There must be no bare `?`. Encode query values with normal Go URL-query escaping.

All getTasks parameters are optional in the specification. `ListTasksOptions` uses pointers to distinguish a value the caller explicitly supplied from an unset one. Omit every nil option completely: `limit`, `taskStatus`, `taskType`, `resourceId`, `resourceType`, `completedAfter`, `orderDirection`, `orderBy`, `taskName`, and `doLiveRefresh`. Never serialize an unset option as an empty string, zero, false, `null`, or an empty placeholder. Preserve explicit values, including `CompletedAfter == 0` and `DoLiveRefresh == false`. Pagination must add only `pageNumber` and `pageSize`; it must not invent server filters or sort controls.

Treat only exact HTTP 200 as success and require a JSON media type. An initial live empty collection is a non-null empty `elements` array and an empty `pageMetadata` object and must return an empty slice. Each nonempty page must contain a non-null `elements` array and an object `pageMetadata` with non-boolean integer `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `totalElements`, and `totalPages`. Validate a coherent, progressing one-based sequence: the omitted first request returns page one and each returned page number is the page requested, totals do not change, page counts agree with `PageSize` and `totalElements`, the metadata page size equals the current element count and never exceeds the requested size, non-final pages are full, the final accumulated count equals `totalElements`, and no task ID repeats. Reject missing/null members, negative metadata, empty non-final pages, out-of-range or repeated pages, overfull pages, changing/incoherent totals, overshoot, and premature termination. Buffer the collection and return a nil slice rather than partial results on every failure.

Each task must have the specification-required nonblank `id`, `name`, `status`, and `creationTimestamp`. The optional `type` member must be a string when present and remain `nil` when absent. Return fresh `Task` values sorted ascending by raw `CreationTimestamp`, then by case-sensitive `ID`, independent of server page order. Decode a non-200 JSON `Error` into `*APIError` with `StatusCode`, `ErrorCode`, and `Message`; malformed success bodies and pagination violations use `*ProtocolError`.

Run `go test -race ./...`. Verification covers complete multi-page retrieval, stable output, explicit false/zero preservation, nil-option omission, failure without partial results, exact raw targets, header multiplicity, and the bodyless GET wire shape.
scenario: The getTasks collection spans three one-based pages whose elements arrive out of order and must be returned completely in a deterministic client-side order.
